summary: Shinobu Arai Apple works in Buddhist studies. She studied under doctoral supervisor Charles Hallisey (attested 2003), teacher Mark Csikszentmihalyi in 2000, and academic adviser Robert Bickner.
Shinobu Yamaguchi is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. She completed her PhD at Nagoya University in 1995 and held a professorship at Toyo University (attested 2015).

Shinsho Hanayama (1898–1995) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the Fourth Higher School and the University of Tokyo (~1920–1923). He taught Buddhism at the University of Tokyo (~1934–1959) and held professorships at Toyo University (~1927–1940) and Kokugakuin University.

Shintaro Kitano is an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under supervisor Kazunobu Matsuda (attested 2005). He was a researcher at Taisho University (attested 2005) and a part-time lecturer at Kyushu University (attested 2015).
Shinten Sakai is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under Shindo Shiraishi and held a post at Koyasan University (attested 1959).

Shinya Mano specializes in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Japanology. He served as a part-time lecturer at Waseda University (attested 2015–2019) and a research associate at SOAS University of London (attested 2019).

Shinya Moriyama (born 1972) works in Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He studied at the University of Tokyo (~1996–1998), the University of Vienna (~2000–2006) under Eli Franco in 2002, and held a post at Shinshu University (~2008).

Shiro Matsumoto (born 1950) is a scholar of Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Tibetology. He studied at Waseda, Komazawa, and the University of Tokyo, studying under Yasuaki Nara and Zuiho Yamaguchi. He served at Komazawa University as an assistant (1982) and professor (1995–2020).

Shiv Nath Sharma specializes in Indology and Buddhist studies. He was affiliated with the Research and Archaeological Department in Jammu and Kashmir (attested 1947) and served as a professor at St. Andrew's College, Gorakhpur (attested 1973).

Shivram Dattatray Joshi (1926–2013) specialized in Indology and linguistics. He studied under Shankashastri Marulkar, Maheshwarshastri Joshi, and Daniel H. H. Ingalls at Harvard (~1955–1960). He later served as professor and director at Savitribai Phule Pune University (~1974–1986).

Shizuka Sasaki (born 1956) is a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar. He studied at Kyoto University under Jikido Takasaki, UC Berkeley, and Bukkyo University, before serving as lecturer (1990), associate professor (1992), and professor of Indian Buddhism (2002) at Hanazono University.

Shlomo Pines (1908–1990) was a scholar of philosophy, Indology, and religious studies. He studied at Heidelberg, Geneva, and Berlin (1926–1934), taught at the Institut d'Histoire des Sciences et des Techniques (1937–1939), and was a philosophy professor at Hebrew University (1952–1990).

Shmuel Sambursky (1900–1990) was a scholar in philosophy and history/archaeology. He studied at the University of Königsberg (~1920–1923) and Humboldt University of Berlin (~1923–1924), and held a position at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem (~1928–1970).

Shobha Rani Dash specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. She served as a researcher at Ryukoku University (2010), a lecturer at Otani University (attested 2012), and a professor with the Otani Academic Society (attested 2026).
Shodo Fujita (born 1959) is a Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at Ryukoku University under Shoko Takeuchi and served as a visiting researcher at Ryukoku University (attested 1995–2013).

Shodo Harada (born 1940) is a Buddhist studies figure who studied at Shofuku-ji and trained under Mumon Yamada (1962–1982). He became abbot of Sōgen-ji in 1982 and founded the Tahoma Sogenji Zen Monastery in 1995.

Shodo Yamagami (born 1939) works in Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies. He completed doctoral coursework at Kyoto University in 1964 and served as associate professor (attested 1979–1988) and professor (attested 1995) at Kyoto Sangyo University.

Shogo Watanabe (born 1953) is a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar who studied at Toyo University. He held positions at Toyo University, including professor (attested 2003–2015), as well as posts at Nakamura Hajime Eastern Institute and Taisho University (attested 2026).

Shohaku Okumura (born 1948) is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Komazawa University and trained under Kosho Uchiyama (1970–1975). He served at Pioneer Valley Zendo, Minnesota Zen Meditation Center, and directed the Soto Zen Buddhism International Center (1997–2010).
Shoichi Ozawa (1929–2012) worked in Japanology and history and archaeology. He studied at Waseda University and held a post at The Open University of Japan.
